deep.reconstruction:
Context: an axiomatic development of 'espaces modérés' (tame spaces) satisfying axioms (M1)_0, (M2), (M3), (M4), ..., (M10). The previous page shows that tameness of maps is local, so tame maps form a sheaf and the tame structure is determined by the sheaf of germs of tame real-valued functions. The struck-out first line ('l'ind-modérés loc. sépt') suggests the ambient category Esp_Mo is a category of ind-tame (or 'locally separated ind-tame') spaces, i.e. spaces glued or filtered from tame pieces. This page defines the full subcategory of locally tame spaces.

Definition (reconstructed). An object X of Esp_Mo is locally tame if:
(i) its topology is Hausdorff;
(ii) every point has a neighbourhood that is tame (as a subspace);
(iii) every point has a fundamental system of tame neighbourhoods;
(iv) the compact subsets of X are exactly the subsets contained in some tame part.

Condition (iv) indicates that in this axiomatics tame spaces behave like compact objects (compact polyhedra, compact semialgebraic or definable sets). Hence 'compact' means 'bounded by a tame piece', and the tame parts form a cofinal system among the compacta. This is the tame analogue of 'locally compact + compactly generated'.

Example: by axiom (M10), R^n is locally tame (not tame, since it is not compact). Some further class of R-spaces (illegible, perhaps open subsets of R^n) is also locally tame.

Claim: locally tame spaces form a full subcategory Esploc_Mo of Esp_Mo stable under finite limits.
- Finite products: products of tame neighbourhoods are tame, and compacts of a product lie in products of compacts.
- Fibre products and equalisers: closed subspaces of a Hausdorff locally tame space are again locally tame, provided tame parts are stable under fibre products, which is presumably one of the (M)-axioms.

Marginal note: an intended lemma, 'say that a compact [and ...] part of a tame neighbourhood is tame?', with a cross-reference ('Voir'). The purpose is the familiar step of passing from 'tame compact neighbourhood' to compact subsets inside it.
errors: The marginal statement, if read literally as 'any compact part of a tame neighbourhood is tame', is false in every usual model (semialgebraic, subanalytic, o-minimal): a Cantor set is a compact subset of [0,1] but is not tame. It must be restricted, e.g. to compact parts that are tame-constructible or closed tame parts. Grothendieck seems aware of a problem, since the note is phrased as a question with a deletion.

Condition (iv) ('compacts = parts contained in a tame part') presupposes that tame parts are compact. That is consistent only if Esp_Mo's basic tame objects are compact. Otherwise R^n itself would be tame and the example would be vacuous. This is a convention to be fixed, not a contradiction.

Stability under finite limits is asserted without proof. It requires that tame parts be stable under finite products and closed tame subobjects, and Hausdorffness for equalisers to be closed. This is plausible given the axioms but not checked on the page.

ideas.what: Locally tame spaces: Hausdorff spaces with fundamental systems of tame neighbourhoods, whose compacta are the subsets of tame parts; a full subcategory of (ind-)tame spaces.
ideas.modern_name: Locally semialgebraic / locally definable spaces; also weakly semialgebraic spaces as the ind-version
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs & Knebusch (Locally Semialgebraic Spaces, LNM 1173, 1985); Knebusch (Weakly Semialgebraic Spaces, LNM 1367, 1989); for o-minimal structures Edmundo, Peterzil and others (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5) and in Récoltes et Semailles; the specific definition is not published as far as I know (unsure).

ideas.what: Stability of locally tame spaces under finite limits (full subcategory of Esp_Mo closed under finite projective limits).
ideas.modern_name: Closure of locally definable / locally semialgebraic spaces under fibre products

ideas.what: Characterising compacta as subsets of tame parts (tame pieces cofinal among compacts): the 'compactly generated by tame pieces' picture, linking ind-tame objects to locally tame spaces.
ideas.modern_name: Admissible coverings / 'locally definable spaces are directed unions of definable pieces'; compactly generated spaces

missed.claim: The page (with the struck 'ind-modérés') sets up, in an axiomatic tame-topology framework, the passage from tame (compact) spaces to ind-tame spaces and to locally tame spaces as a full subcategory stable under finite limits. This anticipates by about a decade the categorical structure of Delfs–Knebusch's locally semialgebraic spaces and Knebusch's weakly semialgebraic spaces, and later locally definable spaces in o-minimality. It does so axiomatically, independent of a particular structure. The historical link (Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics preceding the Knebusch school) is not documented in the literature as far as I know. Mathematically, the content is standard today.
missed.quote: Les espaces loc. modérés forment une sous-catégorie pleine Esploc_Mo de Esp_Mo, stable par lim finies.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck had worked out the basic ind/local categorical layer of tame topology in the 1970s, before the semialgebraic and o-minimal literature. It is relevant to assessments of the 'Esquisse' tame-topology programme.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine definition of locally tame spaces inside an axiomatic tame-topology setting. It is historically interesting as an early, independent anticipation of locally and weakly semialgebraic spaces, but it contains no result that would surprise a specialist today.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck text reads approximately 'l'ind-modérés loc. sépt' (struck), so the ambient category appears to be ind-tame spaces.
'qui forment dans un sens plus explicit' should more plausibly read '-- qui forment donc un ensemble cofinal dans celui des parties compactes' (tame parts cofinal among compacts).
'Par exemple, pour (M10)' should probably read 'Par exemple, par (M10)'.
'ainsi les R^n modérés' is uncertain; the image shows something like 'ainsi que les R^F ouverts[?]'.
Struck after 'loc. modérés' is 'Esploc_Mo' (with a crossed symbol), then 'forment une sous-catégorie pleine Esploc_Mo de Esp_Mo, stable par lim finies'.
Margin: reads approximately 'Dire que toute partie compacte et [struck word] d'un voisinage modéré est modérée — Voir ...', followed by a short illegible word at the bottom.
